name: Tomato-Watermelon Salad

cookwares.name: wire rack and rimmed baking sheet

instructions.primary_message: Juice the lime. Thinly slice the shallot crosswise into rounds. Quarter the cocktail tomatoes. Halve the red cherry tomatoes. Cut the seedless watermelon into 3/4-inch cubes. Crumble the sheep’s milk feta cheese. Tear the mint leaves.
instructions.secondary_message:
½ lime, divided
1 small shallot
285 g cocktail tomatoes
170 g red cherry tomatoes
1.4 kg seedless watermelon
113 g sheep’s milk feta cheese
3 tbsp fresh mint leaves

instructions.primary_message: In a medium non-reactive bowl, whisk together vinegar, lime juice, honey, and 3/4 teaspoon salt. Stir in shallot and let sit for 10 minutes. Whisk in oil, lime zest, and serrano.
Toss cocktail and cherry tomatoes in dressing and let sit at room temperature to marinate for 30 minutes, gently tossing occasionally.

While the cocktail and cherry tomatoes marinate, place the heirloom tomato slices on a wire rack set over a rimmed baking sheet and sprinkle evenly with remaining 1/4 teaspoon salt. Let sit for 10 minutes. Pour any accumulated tomato juices into the dressing mixture.

Arrange heirloom tomato slices on a serving platter. Gently toss watermelon cubes with cocktail and cherry tomatoes and dressing; using a slotted spoon, spoon tomato and watermelon salad over heirloom tomato slices. Sprinkle with feta, mint, and flaky salt. Serve immediately with the remaining marinade/dressing on the side for drizzling.

description: This vibrant summer salad pairs juicy watermelon and tomatoes with creamy feta, fragrant mint, and a tangy dressing with lime, honey, shallots, and chiles.
notes:
Total time, including resting: 50 min.

Optional or for serving: 1 serrano chile (about 14 g; 15 g), seeded if desired, and thinly sliced crosswise (optional); Flaky sea salt, for serving

Optional substitutions: red cherry tomatoes → multicolored cherry tomatoes

Notes: Cocktail tomatoes are small tomatoes on the vine, roughly the size of a golf ball. Any small heirloom tomato will work well here. If you can't find them, you can simply use additional cherry tomatoes.

Make-ahead and storage: This salad is best eaten fresh, but it can sit at room temperature for up to 4 hours, or be refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 1 day. Note that as it sits, excess liquid will puddle on the bottom.
author: Leah Colins
